summary: Feed s134_double to IDS is degraded: 80.6% encrypted traffic exceeds 60% IDS tolerance and 30.6% ERSPAN-tunneled frames hide inner payloads, both blinding signature and payload inspection.

findings.root_cause: 81% of bytes are encrypted (TLS/encrypted) vs IDS tolerance of 60%. Traffic is not being decrypted before the IDS, so payload is opaque.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS needs full payload for signature matching; with 80.6% encrypted it cannot inspect content, missing intrusions, malware and C2 inside encrypted streams.

recommended_fix.why: Decrypt or selectively forward decrypted traffic via packet broker TLS visibility solution so IDS receives cleartext it can analyze; alternatively filter/route encrypted traffic to dedicated decryption zone.

findings.root_cause: 30.6% of frames (606/1983) arrive encapsulated in ERSPAN tunnel. Packet broker is forwarding ERSPAN without stripping header, so IDS sees outer tunnel only.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS parses outer ERSPAN header and misses inner L2-L7 headers and payload; flow correlation, signatures and detection for tunneled traffic fail, creating 30% visibility gap.

recommended_fix.why: Configure packet broker to terminate/strip ERSPAN encapsulation and present inner original frames to IDS so it can parse true endpoints and payloads.
